title: Individual Unemployability Months in a Disability Compensation Decision Past-Due
content:
**Rule.** The standing months of a Disability Compensation decision past-due paid at the individual unemployability rate are:

- every standing month, when individual unemployability is granted and the whole months from its effective date to the issue date of the most recent monthly payment, less one for each payment that came back and has no replacement, are at least the standing months;
- that many months alone, the others at the veteran-alone rate, when they are fewer;
- none, when the decision history shows no individual unemployability granted.

A standing month at the individual unemployability rate takes that rate, 3938.58, in place of the veteran-alone rate, and its additions from the 100 percent tier — spouse 220.30, spouse aid and attendance 201.41, child 146.10, school child 472.95, parent 176.88. Any other standing month takes its additions from the award's own tier.

Individual unemployability's effective date is the effective date on the most recent rating decision granting it; the months counted from it never fall below nothing.

**Input — judgement — output (hypothetical award at Disability Compensation (80% Combined Rating), 6 standing months, no dependents)**

- *Input:* individual unemployability effective 10 October 2025; most recent monthly payment issued 1 April 2026; one payment came back with no replacement.
- *Judgement:* whole months from 10 October 2025 to 1 April 2026 are 5; less 1 open return, 4; 4 is fewer than 6.
- *Output:* 4 standing months at 3938.58 and 2 at the 80 percent veteran-alone rate of 2102.15: 15754.32 plus 4204.30, that is 19958.62 for the entitlement the decisions support.

Had the whole months less open returns been 6 or more, all 6 standing months would be at 3938.58; with no individual unemployability on record, all 6 would be at 2102.15.
